methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: The Power of Contrast
content: Problem: Students can describe a single place or object, but lack the connecting words to compare two different things in one fluid thought.

Solution: We introduce the conjunction "but" to show contrast. By comparing two distinctly different environments (Farm vs. City), students naturally practice pairing opposing adjectives (noisy/quiet, busy/peaceful) and connecting two independent clauses.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
content: Session 1: Introduce the farm setting and basic contrasts (city vs. farm, noisy vs. quiet).
Session 2: Focus on farm animals (cow, chicken, pig) and what exists in each place.
Session 3: Consolidate the environments (countryside, field, fresh air) and express personal preferences using "but".

methodology.title: 2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Ask the student: "Is the city quiet?" -> Student: "The city is noisy, but the farm is quiet."
S2 pull-out: Ask the student: "What animals are on the farm?" -> Student: "There are cows, chickens, and pigs."
Communicative task (Section 8): Information Gap. Students debate and compare two pictures (one of a city, one of a farm) to find differences.

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W10: farm, countryside, peaceful, clean, fresh
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: "but" for contrast
instructions: Grammar focus this week: "but" for contrast.

Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.
